region: Sagaponack · The Hamptons, Long Island, New York
about: Wölffer Estate sits on former potato fields in Sagaponack, on Long Island’s South Fork. Hamburg-born Christian Wölffer bought his first 14 acres here in 1978 and planted the vineyard in 1988; since his death in 2008 the estate has been run by his children, Marc and Joey Wölffer. Winemaker and partner Roman Roth has made the wines since 1992, and the estate’s 55 acres of vines are certified by Long Island Sustainable Winegrowing.

Cabernet Franc is often called Long Island’s signature red, ripening reliably in the island’s long, moderate maritime season. This bottling belongs to Wölffer’s Gold Label range, meant to show the South Fork’s cool Atlantic terroir at an everyday price. The 2023 is mostly Cabernet Franc, rounded out with small amounts of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and a touch of Petit Verdot, and it is made and bottled at the estate in Sagaponack.

Wölffer describes a dark purple, medium-bodied wine with notes of cassis, figs, licorice, leather and toasted sandalwood, velvety tannins and fresh acidity. Wine Enthusiast’s Christina Pickard found violets, fresh berries and a savory edge over a creamy, mid-weight palate. The winery suggests serving it slightly below room temperature, and it is a natural partner for wood-fired meats.
facts: 82% Cabernet Franc, 11% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Sauvignon, 1% Petit Verdot
